expected.report:
SPECIMEN:
(A) Ascending colon polyp
(B) caecal polyp 12 mm
(C) Rectum polyp

MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION:
(A)  Sections show large intestinal mucosa with architecturally distorted serrated crypts, which show basal dilatation and serration extending into the crypt bases, in keeping with a sessile serrated lesion / adenoma. No cytological dysplasia is identified. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy. The lesion is completely excised in the planes examined.

(B)  Sections show large intestinal mucosa with architecturally distorted serrated crypts, which show basal dilatation and serration extending into the crypt bases, in keeping with a sessile serrated lesion / adenoma. There is a focus of high grade dysplasia of intestinal (adenomatous) type, showing cribriform and back-to-back glands, loss of polarity with full-thickness nuclear stratification and markedly enlarged nuclei with prominent nucleoli. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy.

(C)  Sections show a polypoid piece of large intestinal mucosa with villiform architecture, slit-like serrations and ectopic crypt foci, lined by tall columnar cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and pencillate nuclei, in keeping with a traditional serrated adenoma. There is a focus of high grade dysplasia of intestinal (adenomatous) type, showing cribriform and back-to-back glands, loss of polarity with full-thickness nuclear stratification and markedly enlarged nuclei with prominent nucleoli. There is no evidence of invasive malignancy. The base is not clearly represented.

DIAGNOSIS:
(A) ASCENDING COLON, Ascending colon polyp, polypectomy - SESSILE SERRATED LESION / ADENOMA.
(B) CAECUM, caecal polyp 12 mm, polypectomy - SESSILE SERRATED LESION / ADENOMA with HIGH GRADE DYSPLASIA.
(C) RECTUM, Rectum polyp, polypectomy - TRADITIONAL SERRATED ADENOMA with HIGH GRADE DYSPLASIA.
